accepted-story-continuity.state-bridge: S01 ended after Mara disrupted Livia's nonverbal calibration by controlling the cues others were reading. Most apparent accuracy collapsed, while Jonah's precisely timed wrist pressure and recognition remained unexplained. Mara chose to continue at Fulcrum as an experiment; she is attracted to Jonah and still uncertain whether she belongs.
accepted-story-continuity.use: Factual continuity only; it is not a prose exemplar.

activation-conditions.item: Two characters negotiate fear, desire, care, or authority.

creative-obligations.item: Use contemporary American speech particular to Mara, Livia, Miriam, and Jonah; pair it with body language that changes the exchange.

activation-conditions.item: Another character's motive is consequential but not directly knowable.

activation-conditions.item: Physical position or attraction must become vivid.

activation-conditions.item: A relational claim would become generic if explained directly.

creative-obligations.item: Let one concrete action carry an emotional claim and alter the next available choice.

author-subgenre-delta.item: Emotion moves through dialogue joined to specific physical action.
Sensory detail establishes logistics and relationship meaning at the same time.
Intimacy belongs to these characters' history and changes what they can choose next.
Plain concrete prose makes rare lyrical release more forceful.

item.text:
He came closer, a tall naked ghost, smelling of sleep.
“I always wake when you do, Sassenach; I sleep ill without ye by my side.” He touched my forehead briefly. “I thought ye were maybe fevered; the bed was damp where ye’d lain. You’re sure you’re all right?”
“I was hot; I couldn’t sleep. But yes, I’m all right. And you?” I touched his face; his skin was warm with sleep.
He came to stand beside me at the window, looking out into the late summer night. The moon was full, and the birds were restless; from near at hand, I heard the faint chirp of a late-nesting warbler.
item.transfer: Study the economy: dialogue, touch, temperature, position, and a single setting detail do several jobs at once. Transpose the mechanism into contemporary American English; do not copy names, dialect, setting, plot, or wording.

item.text:
A hand touched her face, big and very gentle.
“You’re a fine, braw lassie,” he whispered. “But a lassie, nonetheless. Would ye fret your heart out and think yourself a coward because ye couldna fight off a lion wi’ your bare hands? It’s the same. Dinna be daft, now.”
She wiped the back of her hand under her nose, and sniffed deeply.
He put a hand under her elbow and helped her up, his strength no longer either threat or mockery, but unutterable comfort. Her knees stung, where she had scraped them on the ground. Her legs wobbled, but she made it to the haypile, where he let her sit down.
“You could have just told me, you know.”
item.transfer: Study how a small action changes the emotional meaning of strength and makes the final line sharper. Transpose that causal craft only; do not copy names, dialect, setting, plot, or wording.

negative-space.item: The source sample is deliberately tiny; treat its affordances as provisional rather than a complete author model.
Do not import source names, plots, historical setting, Scots dialect, signature phrases, or scene sequence.
Do not replace scene causality with generalized therapeutic validation.

contradictions.item: She wants to be seen completely and resents any claim to see her without permission.
Her inherited caution can sharpen perception or disguise fear; the story must keep both live.

invariants.item: Sheltered but formidable: inexperience does not imply stupidity or passivity.
Highly observant, especially when status and goodness are being made to conflict.
Treats desire as morally significant without treating it as either an enemy or a command.
Her courage becomes clearest when she can preserve ambiguity and still choose.

adrian-voss.item: Is vulnerable to his flattering fusion of virtue, competence, and world-historical need.
Tests his system before she is ready to oppose his authority.

jonah-reed.item: Becomes more sensually alert when Jonah protects her freedom without advertising the protection.
Trust begins through shared perception and humor, not extracted confession.

livia-sloane.item: Feels attraction, admiration, rivalry, and epistemic caution at once.
Wants Livia's skill to be real without granting it unlimited interpretive authority.

contradictions.item: She wants to free people from self-deception and also wants to own the pace of their disclosure.
A mundane cue mechanism explains some successes without exhausting her skill or the scene's mystery.

invariants.item: Sensuous, brilliant, wounded, agentic, and genuinely skilled.
Her care is real even when she uses care as leverage.
Redemption remains possible without erasing the costs of her choices.

item.name: Livia Sloane

jonah-reed.item: Finds his refusal to perform others both attractive and obstructive.
Tests whether his irony conceals conviction.

mara-vale.item: Experiences Mara as a delightful talent, a possible intimate, and a threat to Fulcrum's status economy.
Offers genuine initiation while testing whether Mara will surrender interpretive sovereignty.

item.role: friend-rival and Fulcrum's most gifted attention reader

contradictions.item: His restraint can express courageous regard or function as an elegant way to evade responsibility.
Social ease gives him room to resist Fulcrum while also cushioning him from its costs.

invariants.item: Playful, patient, and socially fluent without being socially owned.
His erotic appeal depends on attention, restraint, apology, and protected freedom.
He can see accurately without turning perception into possession or performance.

item.name: Jonah Reed

livia-sloane.item: Respects her skill and resists the entitlement she builds around it.
Avoids a direct contest until that avoidance begins to impose a cost on others.

mara-vale.item: Refuses to narrate her for the room.
Recognizes her silent control and lets shared perception carry the first connection.

item.role: romantic counterpart and hardware security researcher

item.observable-mechanism: A small pause makes thought, dream, urge, and bodily sensation available to judgment instead of command.
Silence is an active complement to speech and a condition for language that is awake, loving, and true.
Blinking, hesitancy, fidgeting, smiles, tempo, and emphasis can be recruited as signs of an internal clash—especially by an observer.
Near-synonyms can evoke different concepts and bodily responses; a method can confuse word-choice effects with discovery of hidden truth.

scene-state.desire: Mara wants to preserve friendship with Livia, keep her place on the project, and understand the humiliating bodily reaction she had during the exercise.
scene-state.obstacle: Every attempt to leave is interpreted as evidence that she needs to stay. Her breath, posture, hesitation, and attraction to Jonah are read aloud as hidden content.
scene-state.opening-image: Near the end of an overlong alignment session, genuine care has made an ordinary attempt to stop socially and institutionally costly.

pressure-ladder.item: spiritualized claim that refusal harms the group.

scene-state.title: The Doorway Rule

story-contract.heat: High embodied attention without graphic anatomy or consummation. The mutually wanted kiss stops while still desired.
story-contract.pov: Close third-person Mara; no sustained access to other minds.
story-contract.relationship: Adult monogamous slow burn toward marriage; attraction must increase freedom, perception, trust, and meaningful choice.
story-contract.world-status: Keep ordinary and extraordinary explanations live. Do not confirm either paranormal causation or its absence.
